summary: Specifies how to signal pseudowire status messages over an associated channel, for static pseudowires that have no dynamic control plane. It also updates RFC 5885 when BFD is used for status signaling. It was later updated by RFC 7274.

eli5.summary: Some tunnels are set up by hand, without a chat system to report trouble. This gives them a side channel for sending status messages like "I'm down".

questions: how does pw status signaling work
what is the pw oam message
subtitle: How hand-configured pseudowires tell each other about faults, using a side channel in the data path.

tldr.problem: A static pseudowire has no control plane, so the two edge devices at its ends have no way to tell each other that the pseudowire or its attachment circuit has failed.
tldr.mechanism: Status codes are carried in a PW OAM message (associated channel type 0x0027) sent in-band with the pseudowire data and repeated until acknowledged or refreshed on a timer.
tldr.outcome: Static pseudowires gain status signaling, OAM message mapping and redundancy. The RFC updates RFC 5885 and was itself later updated by RFC 7274.

today: RFC 6478 is a Proposed Standard. It updates RFC 5885 and has itself been updated by RFC 7274.

sections.title: The Problem With Static Pseudowires
sections.content:
The default control plane for a pseudowire (PW) is the Label Distribution Protocol (LDP), as defined in RFC 4447. That RFC also describes a static provisioning mode with no control plane. On a static PW there is no method to send the status of the PW or its attachment circuit (AC) between the two Provider Edge (PE) devices at its ends.

RFC 6478 defines a way to carry the PW status codes from RFC 4447 in-band with the PW data, using a generic associated channel from RFC 5586. The mechanism also fits where a Terminating PE (T-PE) needs to send a status message directly to the far-end T-PE.
sections.eli5: If a tunnel is set up by hand, nobody tells you when the other end breaks. This RFC adds a way to send that news along the tunnel itself.

sections.title: When to Use It
sections.content:
A PE that sets up an MPLS PW by means other than LDP, such as static configuration, MUST support some alternative method of status reporting. This RFC supplies one for statically configured PWs where no LDP control plane is available.

A PE that sets up a PW with LDP MUST use the PW status TLV mechanism and MUST NOT use this one on that PW, to avoid duplicate or conflicting notifications. The one exception is the optional S-PE bypass mode, which can be used when both T-PEs establish the PW with LDP.

For the same reason, the BFD VCCV status-signaling mechanisms of RFC 5885 (CV Types 0x08 and 0x20) MUST NOT be used alongside this protocol. BFD VCCV for fault detection (CV types 0x04 and 0x10) MAY still be used.
sections.eli5: If a tunnel already has its own way to report trouble, do not use two reporters at once, or they might contradict each other.

sections.title: The PW OAM Message
sections.content:
The PW status TLV from RFC 4447 travels inside a PW OAM message on the PW associated channel. The message starts with the standard associated channel header: a first nibble of 0001, a version and reserved value both set to 0, and the code point 0x0027 for PW OAM Message.

After that come a refresh timer, a TLV length covering all TLVs, and an A flag followed by reserved flags. The refresh timer is in seconds, from 1 to 65535. The value 0 means infinity: the message is never refreshed and never times out. The remaining flag bits MUST be 0 on transmit and ignored on receipt.

The PW status TLV itself uses type 0x096A. Unlike in RFC 4447, its first 2 bits are reserved: MUST be zero on transmit and ignored on receipt. Only this TLV is defined for now, though other TLVs may be defined later from the IANA "LDP TLV Type Name Space".
sections.eli5: It is a short note with a timer saying how often to repeat it, a box to tick for "got it", and the actual status report.

sections.title: Sending, Refreshing and Acknowledging
sections.content:
There is no TCP/IP session here, so each message must be sent repeatedly to be delivered reliably. A message with a new status bit set or cleared is sent immediately. If it is not acknowledged within a second, it is repeated twice more at one-second intervals, and after that it is sent at the interval given by its refresh timer. The suggested default refresh timer is 600 seconds.

A receiver starts a timer from the refresh rate in the packet. If no new non-zero status message arrives within 3.5 times that value, the status times out and the default status of zero is assumed. To clear a fault, the sender simply sends a message with the bit cleared. For a status code of zero, transmission stops after 3 messages at one-second intervals.

A receiver MAY acknowledge by replying with the same format and status code and the A bit set. It MAY use the refresh timer field to request a new interval, at most once per refresh interval. The sender can refuse by refreshing with the timer value it wants. PW OAM status messages MUST NOT be used as a connectivity verification method.
sections.eli5: You keep repeating your message until someone says "got it", then you repeat it every so often as a reminder. If the reminders stop for too long, the other side assumes everything is fine again.

sections.title: Label Stack and S-PE Bypass Mode
sections.content:
Normally a status message goes to the adjacent PE across the PSN tunnel, with the PW label TTL set to 1. If the control word is not in use, the PE MUST also place the GAL reserved label from RFC 5586 below the PW label with TTL 1.

In S-PE bypass mode, a T-PE that uses LDP sends a message straight to the T-PE at the other end, skipping every switching PE (S-PE). It sets the PW label TTL high enough to reach that T-PE, according to local policy. The mode is optional and both T-PEs MUST support it.

Only four status codes may be sent this way: 0x00000002, 0x00000004, 0x00000020 and 0x00000040. "Clear all failures" MUST NOT be sent, because an S-PE may send it too. Messages received by bypass take priority over those from LDP, but the same status MUST also be sent in LDP to keep the S-PEs updated. A T-PE requests the mode with the B bit in the PW Generic Protocol Flags sub-TLV (type 0x18, length 4).
sections.eli5: Usually you pass the message to your next neighbor. In bypass mode you mail it straight to the far end, skipping the stops in between, but only for a few kinds of news.

sections.title: Switching Between Segments
sections.content:
A switching PE (S-PE) follows the procedures of RFC 6073. When a static PW segment is switched to another static segment, the LDP header is simply replaced by the PW OAM header, and the packet format is otherwise identical. The information needed for an SP-PE TLV MUST be configured on the S-PE, or none is sent. A new switching point TLV type 0x07 (length 24) carries the Static PW/MPLS-TP PW segment ID of the last segment traversed.

When a dynamic LDP segment meets a static one and the LDP label is withdrawn by the adjacent PE, the S-PE sets status code 0x00000001, Pseudowire Not Forwarding, on the static segment.
sections.eli5: When a hand-made tunnel connects to a self-managed one, the middle device translates the news from one to the other.

sections.title: Security and IANA Notes
sections.content:
The security measures in RFC 4447, RFC 5085 and RFC 6073 are described as adequate for this mechanism. No new security text is added.

IANA set up a registry of "PW Generic Protocol Flags", 16-bit strings. Bit 0 is S-PE bypass mode and bits 1 through 15 are assigned by IETF Review. IANA also assigned the associated channel type 0x0027, the switching point TLV type 0x07 and the interface parameter type 0x18.
sections.eli5: The safety rules of the older systems are considered good enough, and a few official numbers were reserved for the new pieces.
